hook: What if AI reverse-engineering games is the *start of something much bigger*?
caption:
AI is starting to automate one of the most difficult parts of software development: reverse engineering.
Jaden Williams' viral video points to a new wave of AI-assisted game modding where coding agents can inspect existing software, decompile parts of it, identify how it works and help build working modifications.
Tools like Universal Modder now connect agents including Claude Code and Codex with reverse-engineering software such as Ghidra and ILSpy.
The security implications are more nuanced than the video's "death of software" framing.
Making software easier to understand could lower the barrier to finding weaknesses or copying functionality, but reverse engineering a program is very different from breaking modern cryptography or automatically compromising secure systems.
What happens when understanding someone else's software becomes an AI task?
